findings.summary: The change adds a ContactRecord invariant that private notes are never exported, but in the same change the export operation and the export journey both say each exported contact includes its private notes.
findings.evidence: entity.ContactRecord invariants: "Private notes are never included in an export" vs operation.data.export effects: "Each exported contact includes its private notes" and J.control.export x4: "Export authorized records of the authenticated owner only, with each contact's private notes"

findings.summary: The Export affordance's effects were not updated to match the changed export operation, so the UI-level description of export no longer matches what the operation does.
findings.evidence: affordance.ExportControls.export effects: [Export authorized records of the authenticated owner only] vs operation.data.export effects: [..., Each exported contact includes its private notes, ...]

findings.summary: The criterion now checks the private notes column, but its hook fixture still covers only owner and version constraints, so the new claim has no executable evidence.
findings.evidence: claim: "Checks owner and version constraints, the private notes column and authorized persistence..." vs hook inputs fixture: "owner and version constraints via binding.contactsStore"
